title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore Auditorium on 1966-01-08

ai_review.summary: Rare early‑1966 Fillmore Acid Test soundboard capture – raw and fair in fidelity but historically priceless, featuring a tight blues‑driven set with Jerry’s fire‑spitting guitar.
ai_review.review: This recording preserves one of the first Grateful Dead appearances at an Acid Test, delivering surprisingly tight playing for a band that hadn’t even been together a year. Reviewers rave about the blazing blues work, especially Jerry’s Guild tone, and historic moments like “Caution” and “Can't Come Down,” while noting the tape is raw and low‑fi. Despite its technical roughness, the show’s energy and significance make it a must‑hear for Deadheads.

ai_rating.rationale: The vast majority of reviews award five stars and praise the performance; only one overtly negative review exists. Recording quality is noted as raw/fair, but the musical impact and historic value drive a strong overall rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Early tape is raw and low‑fidelity with occasional dropouts; not a polished mix but captures the performance clearly enough for historical listening.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Early Acid Test set balances experimental jams with surprisingly tight blues numbers; the band stays cohesive despite the psychedelic atmosphere.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for straight‑ahead blues playing, 'spitting fire' on his old Guild guitar and delivering a blazing tone.
